correctness.rationale: All finite n>=2: bottom- and join-preservation yield monotonicity; extensive idempotents are uniquely upper ceilings of endpoint-containing fixed sets. If both maps have exclusive fixed points in a common gap, applying the opposite ceiling to the lower exclusive point produces an illegal common fixed point under commutation. If only one map has exclusive gap points, both composites round that gap to its upper common endpoint. This proves the biconditional and equality with the common-fixed-set ceiling. Independent weighted-composition counting yields b_n and its rational generating function. All ordered pairs were exhaustively compared with the criterion for n=2,...,9 in the supplied checker; the infinite family is justified deductively.

originality.rationale: The new mathematical object is the set of ordered commuting pairs of normal S4-style closures of a finite Gödel chain, not a class of single idempotents or the already known numerical sequence A007070. Comparisons of the full motivating 2026 article, the full readable 2019 semigroup article and the OEIS entry found no statement of the exact common-fixed-gap criterion and its application to two modalities. Priority uncertainty about general older commuting-idempotent results remains, but no specific dominating result was identified.

value.rationale: The exact local gap criterion classifies all ordered commuting normal S4 closure modes on every finite Gödel chain. It gives an explicit representation of an interaction equation, an all-size enumerator, and exponential rarity compared to arbitrary pairs. This is a natural full classification of a modal-algebraic interaction, not an arbitrary slice or bare known-table recomputation; reuse of an already known sequence is fully disclosed.
